The Gilbert has also hosted a state-wide original playwriting competition, staged readings, workshops, a children's puppet show, and a special performance for blind/non-sighted audiences. Matt Lamb became Artistic Director in 2025.

name: Little Theater of Gastonia (LTG)
bio: Little Theater of Gastonia is a non-profit, 501(c)(3) theater that has proudly entertained Gaston County since 1950. As the oldest theater in Gastonia, NC, LTG has a long tradition of producing a wide variety of plays and musicals every season featuring local talent from the community and beyond. LTG's mission is to create an immersive theatrical experience that engages audiences and sparks conversation, reflecting the diversity of the community and the world around it. Auditions are always open call and never pre-cast (unless explicitly stated), with a strong commitment to welcoming performers of all ages, races, genders, orientations, capabilities, and experience levels. LTG's 2025-2026 season was supported by the North Carolina Arts Council and the Gaston Arts Council.

name: The Montford Moppets Youth Shakespeare Company
bio: What began in 2009 as a drama class for a small group of local homeschoolers has evolved into a nonprofit, youth-led theatre company. The Montford Moppets Youth Shakespeare Company gives students in Asheville, NC ages 10-17 the space to ponder difficult topics and take ownership of themselves, their talents, and their artistic ability. The Moppets strive to create innovative performances and educational experiences that connect area youth with each other and the wider community, and are committed to providing a safe space and equal access to Western North Carolina youths of all backgrounds and abilities.

name: Parkway Playhouse
bio: Parkway Playhouse is a historic theatre that's been part of the Burnsville, NC community for 79 years. Originally established in 1947 by Dr. William Raymond Taylor, a professor of drama at the Woman's College of Greensboro (now UNCG), Parkway Playhouse once operated as a summer stock venue and a sponsored extension of the drama departments at UNCG and the University of Miami. In the 1990s, the Playhouse became an independent theater company. Today, nestled in the Appalachian Mountains, Parkway Playhouse is the oldest continually operating summer theater in North Carolina, still producing mainstage productions in the summer while offering theatre education opportunities year-round. Its mission is to strengthen the local community by using the performing arts to uplift and unite neighbors and inspire new ways of looking at the world. As a teaching theater, Parkway Playhouse also runs a Junior program, an Appalachian Playwriting Festival each fall showcasing new work rooted in the region, and the 'Reading Is Alive!' outreach initiative.

name: Backyard Theatre Productions
bio: Backyard Theatre Productions is a theatre company by young people, for young people, aiming to support original works of theatre in the Piedmont Triad region of NC. The company creates a space for creative collaboration between teenagers and young adults, providing an often-overlooked opportunity for students to serve in leadership positions, while writing and producing the unique stories of their generation and giving the stage to Greensboro's emerging theatre-makers. Productions are staged in a literal backyard in Greensboro, an open-air venue with flexible seating that has evolved to occasionally include indoor spaces as the company has grown. The community is small but growing, values ensemble and community-driven art, and keeps tickets always pay-what-you-can with no cost to be part of any production. Past productions include How to Get to Neverland (Summer 2025) and Under the Surface.

name: Summerfield Stage Company
bio: Co-Founders and Co-Artistic Directors Amy Alvino and Elyse Rodriguez met as undergraduate BFA Acting students at Elon University in Fall 2004, reuniting years later in 2021 when they both found themselves living in Summerfield, NC. Discovering that the closest community theatres were 20-30 minutes away — a barrier keeping both potential talent and patrons from participating — they founded Summerfield Stage Company with a clear mission: bring community theatre to the underserved northwest Guilford County area. The company launched its debut production, Ichabod: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow, in October 2023 to five sold-out audiences. Since then, SSC has grown to include a youth program (launched Fall 2024 to expand arts access regardless of family income) and a youth performance troupe called The Starlights. Summerfield Stage Company is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit bringing professional-quality, inclusive, and enriching theatre to Northwest Guilford County communities.

name: Ensemble Stage
bio: Founded in October 2009 in Blowing Rock, Ensemble Stage is the NC High Country's only year-round professional theatre. The company relocated to Banner Elk in 2017, settling into its current intimate 99-seat home in the Historic Banner Elk School. Ensemble Stage has sold more than 25,000 tickets across 500-plus performances, offering a mix of heart-warming comedies, historical dramas, suspense thrillers, comedy farces, and thought-provoking dramas across its Main Stage season. The company also stages live radio-style plays paying homage to golden-age radio classics (complete with live sound effects), a Kids Summer Saturday Theatre Series performed by local college theatre majors, theatre camps and acting classes for youth, and an annual holiday musical variety show, 'A Banner Elk Christmas,' patterned after the Andy Williams and Bing Crosby TV Christmas specials of the 1960s-70s. Ensemble Stage is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit whose mission is threefold: to provide affordable, high-quality live theatre to High Country residents and visitors; to inspire and nurture the imagination and social skills of youths and adults through theatre-based education; and to be an active part of the region's cultural and economic growth.

name: Blue Box Theatre Company
bio: Blue Box Theatre Company is a young, Triangle-based collective of creative artists dedicated to bringing moving stories to life, whether new, old, or borrowed. Blue Box structures each season around a simple wedding rhyme: something old (a reimagined classic text), something new (a premiere of an original script), something borrowed (an adaptation), and something blue (an in-house event to thank and celebrate company members). The company's mission is to dedicate its time and passion to creating a safe, inspiring space for creative artists to hone their craft and find a sense of collaborative community, presenting shows that challenge ideas, center around hope, spark joy, or simply entertain.

name: Spirit Gum Theatre Company
bio: Spirit Gum Theatre Company began when three friends simply wanted to collaborate together on stage; the idea of a modest show grew into the dream of a full theatre company. Its name and playful logo (featuring a mustache) reference spirit gum, the adhesive used in theatre to attach costume prosthetics, capturing the playful, creative spirit that drives the company. Now in its 13th season, Spirit Gum is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to producing high-quality theatre and inspiring local actors and artists in Winston-Salem, funded entirely by its patrons.

name: Triad Pride Performing Arts (Triad Pride Acting Company)
bio: Triad Pride Performing Arts (TPPA) is a vibrant collective of LGBTQ+ individuals and allies dedicated to using the power of performance to entertain, enlighten, and enrich. Advocating for equality and social justice, TPPA champions acceptance and understanding regardless of sexual orientation, gender identity, or physical ability. The organization's programs include adult choruses in SSAA (Upper Voice Chorus), TTBB (Lower Voice Chorus), and SATB formats; the Triad Pride Acting Company (TPAC), now in its 9th season, which showcases productions written or composed by or about members of the LGBTQ+ community; Counterpoint, an outreach chorus spreading positivity and awareness; and Theatre For All, a program providing a safe and accessible environment for individuals with disabilities to perform. TPPA is a non-profit resident organization of the Greensboro Cultural Center, made possible by a significant in-kind contribution from Creative Greensboro, the City of Greensboro's office for arts & culture.

name: 40+ Stage Company
bio: Founded in March 2016, 40+ Stage Company is a Winston-Salem theater company for adults in their middle years and beyond, built around the belief in the transformative power of theater. The company's play selection focuses on issues of intergenerational concern and cultural relevance, aiming to provide actors of all ages with opportunities to perform in meaningful, challenging roles while celebrating and enriching the lives of aging adults. As an amateur company, 40+ Stage Company is committed to the highest standards of performance, staging dramas about real historical figures (including past productions on Helen Keller, Paul Robeson, and the Delany sisters) alongside original works and staged readings. The company also runs an outreach program extending to organizations that provide services and moral support to the aging community.

name: Barn Dinner Theatre
bio: The Barn Dinner Theatre franchise was born in 1964 in Roanoke, Virginia, created by Howard Wolfe and Conley Jones Sr. as the birth of the dinner theater concept. A second location soon opened in Greensboro, NC, and though 27 Barn Dinner Theatre locations eventually opened across the country featuring the same barn design and farm-themed decor, the Greensboro location is the only one still operating today — making it the oldest continuously running dinner theater in the United States, now celebrating over 60 years of 'Dinnertainment.' In the franchise's early days, cast members doubled as wait staff and lived on-site in small shared rooms above the theater; a few notable names, including Mickey Rooney, Robert Blake, and Fannie Flagg, performed there over the years. Today, the original staff living quarters serve as the box office, group sales office, and dressing rooms, with a separate team handling dinner service so the cast can focus on the show. Each evening begins with a Southern-style buffet (roast beef, baked chicken, seasonal sides, and dessert) before the buffet is cleared and the theater's signature 'magic stage' rises from the center of the room for the Broadway-style performance.

name: Carolina Ensemble Theatre (CET)
bio: Carolina Ensemble Theatre (CET) weaves the power of live theatre into the fabric of the communities it serves, creating captivating experiences that inspire, entertain, and enrich the lives of audiences. CET provides work for North Carolinian theatre artists, celebrates regional narratives and storytellers, and tells bold stories that speak powerfully to its place and time in the Piedmont Triad, with a stated vision of becoming a driving force in the development of North Carolina's theatrical identity through partnerships with influential cultural organizations and artists. The company's motto is 'A Community of Artists, A World of Stories.'

name: Lexington Live
bio: Lexington Live Community Theatre is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization whose mission is to educate, enrich, and entertain by engaging and uniting the diverse community of Lexington, NC through the universal appeal of the performing arts. The organization is funded entirely by its generous and supportive patrons, staging its productions in a small theatre in downtown Lexington. Its 2024-2025 season produced six shows with 135 cast and crew members and more than 13,000 volunteer hours contributed to productions.

name: North Carolina Stage Company
bio: North Carolina Stage Company is a 125-seat, off-Broadway style professional theatre producing 4-7 plays per season in the heart of downtown Asheville. Founded in 2001 by Charlie and Angie Flynn-McIver, who returned to their home state after establishing acting and directing careers in New York City, NC Stage is now in its 23rd season. The company has been twice recognized for artistic excellence by the American Theatre Wing and the North Carolina Theatre Conference's George A. Parides Award, and was voted best local theatre for 11 of the past 13 years in the Mountain Xpress Best of WNC Poll. NC Stage has hosted three world premieres, including Stalking the Bogeyman (2013), Curvy Widow, and Brave New World (both 2016). NC Stage is a certified 501(c)(3) nonprofit operating under a Small Professional Theatre Tier 4 contract with Actors' Equity Association and the Union of Professional Actors and Stage Managers in the United States.

name: Southern Appalachian Repertory Theatre (SART)
bio: Southern Appalachian Repertory Theatre (SART) is a professional theatre company in residence at the historic Owen Theatre in Mars Hill, North Carolina. Established in 1975 by director and theatre educator Jim Thomas, SART has produced scores of original works, plays, and musicals over the years, many portraying the rich culture and heritage of Southern Appalachia. Now in its 52nd summer season, the company blends original Appalachian-themed works, world premieres, regional comedies, a Youth Theatre program, and innovative programming such as Music Theatre International's Senior Musicals series (productions designed specifically for performers aged 55 and over) — living out its stated belief that theatre belongs to every age and that talent does not fade, retire, or expire.

name: Carolina Theatre of Greensboro
bio: The Carolina Theatre of Greensboro is a historic, non-profit performing arts venue and community landmark in downtown Greensboro, NC. Rather than producing its own resident theatrical season, the Carolina Theatre presents a wide range of touring and rental programming, including touring musicals, comedy, dance, concerts, classic film screenings, speakers, and community events. The organization is currently engaged in its 'Setting the Stage' capital campaign to secure the theatre's future.

name: Randolph Youth Theater Company (RYTC)
bio: Randolph Youth Theater Company (RYTC) is a non-profit community organization that strives to develop youth theatrically by building self-esteem, encouraging responsibility, inspiring creativity, and developing social skills, alongside showcasing many other talents. Since its establishment in 2004, at least 1,900 young performers have walked across the stage in various RYTC productions. The organization offers students ages 8 to 18 the opportunity to participate in several productions a year, now in its 15th season, and has a significant impact on the lives of young people in Asheboro, Randolph County, and the surrounding area.

name: Neuse Little Theatre (NLT)
bio: Neuse Little Theatre is a beloved community theatre based in Smithfield, NC, recently celebrating over 50 years of sharing a love of theatre with the local community. Now in its 52nd season, NLT stages a full slate of plays and musicals each year at its home venue, affectionately known as 'The Hut,' occasionally using outside venues such as Johnston Community College's Paul A. Johnston Auditorium for larger productions. The organization hosts the John B. Kolcum Scholarship, awarded annually to qualified graduating high school or current college students pursuing theatre arts, and runs a summer drama program for youth. NLT also produces its own podcast, The Neuse Little Podcast, featuring conversations and stories from behind the scenes.

name: The Ansonia Theatre
bio: A non-profit historic theatre nestled in the heart of Uptown Wadesboro, now celebrating 100 years since it first opened on August 3, 1925 as a combination movie and vaudeville house. After closing in the late 20th century as television and mall cinemas drew audiences away, the Ansonia has been lovingly restored and reopened as a community theatre and live performance venue. The theatre is now operated by the Anson County Arts Council (ACAC), founded in 1978, whose mission is to enrich the cultural lives of all people of Anson County by nurturing and supporting excellence in the arts. The Ansonia is listed on the National Register of Historic Places as part of the Wadesboro Downtown Historic District.

name: BNS Productions
bio: BNS Productions is Charlotte's only Black repertory theatre company, creating unforgettable performances, educational programs, and community experiences that celebrate Black stories, inspire conversation, and transform audiences through the power of live theatre. Founded by playwright and director Rory D. Sheriff, BNS Productions creates transformative Black theatre experiences in Charlotte, North Carolina that center culture, courage, history, and community. Through stage productions, educational outreach, youth engagement, and storytelling initiatives, BNS uses the performing arts to spark conversation, connection, and change. Since 2010, the company has staged 25+ productions, reaching 10,000+ audience members and serving 2,000+ students through educational programming, with 100+ community partnerships built along the way.

name: Dayelight LLC
bio: Dayelight LLC is the production company of Brian Daye, a Charlotte-based actor, award-winning playwright, director, and producer. Daye has worked as an experienced theatrical director and writer of new works and established plays since 2007, collaborating with local, regional, national, and international theatrical companies. His solo performance piece 'Hey You / An Afrostereophonic Journey' was selected for the 2018 United Solo Festival in New York City and won Best Playwright and Best Performance at the 2022 PEACH Theatre & Film International Festival in Los Angeles. Through Dayelight LLC, Daye produces original theatrical work, including By Any Other Name: An Opus for James Baldwin, staged at Charlotte's Off-Broadway.

name: Charlotte's Off-Broadway (COB)
bio: Charlotte's Off-Broadway (COB) is a professional home-grown theatre company founded in 2004 by Producing Artistic Director Anne Lambert. Located in the 56-seat COB Black Box Theatre inside the VAPA Center in Uptown Charlotte, COB produces bold contemporary theatre that challenges perspectives, celebrates underrepresented voices, and creates meaningful connections between artists and audiences. Beyond producing its own work, COB provides an affordable, professional home for emerging playwrights, independent artists, and smaller theatre companies — including groups like Dayelight LLC, Hot Mess Productions, and Davidson College Theatre — to develop, rehearse, and present new work. Anne Lambert is a founding member of both Chickspeare and the VAPA Center, and received the Metrolina Theatre Award for Theatre Person of the Year in 2024.

name: Cherryville Little Theatre (CLT)
bio: Cherryville Little Theatre, Inc. is a nonprofit community theatre serving Cherryville, NC and the surrounding Gaston County area. Beyond its mainstage productions, CLT offers a full slate of theatre education programming including acting classes, a 'Little Sprouts' program for young children, and summer camps, alongside a Junior Board of Directors that allows teens to gain service hours and leadership experience while being involved behind-the-scenes. The theatre also hosts an annual Short & Sweet One Act Festival and the Nerdville Mini-Con, a geek-culture convention day held on its stage. CLT is led by a volunteer Board of Directors, several of whom have deep multi-decade ties to the Cherryville community and local government.

name: Market Theatre
bio: Market Theatre believes the arts are for everyone, now celebrating its 10th Anniversary season in Anderson, SC. The company creates accessible experiences, opportunities, and spaces where the community can shape and be shaped by the arts, focusing on three core areas of programming: Education (summer camps, year-round classes, and in-school performances), Outreach (free shows in the park, the 24 Hour Musical, and community tours), and Mainstage Productions (a season of diverse, high-quality in-house plays and musicals offering something for everyone). Market Theatre brings over $500,000 in local economic activity to Anderson annually, engages more than 8,500 people through its programming each year, and has received dozens of awards and honors, including recognition from the SC Theatre Association and Southeastern Theatre Conference. Funding provided in part by the South Carolina Arts Commission and the City of Anderson Accommodations Tax Fund.

name: RiverTowne Players
bio: RiverTowne Players performs at the Historic Masonic Theatre in downtown New Bern, NC, presenting a full season of plays and musicals alongside a robust youth theatre program. In partnership with the Masonic Theatre Preservation Foundation, the company operates the RTP Youth Family Hub, School Performances and Youth Theatre programming, a Young Actors Academy, and the Ruth A. Waters Scholarship. RiverTowne Players brings a mix of large-scale musicals, dramatic plays, and youth/teen productions to the historic stage each season.

name: Waxhaw Community Theatre Company
bio: The Waxhaw Community Theatre Company is proud to provide theatrical experiences and opportunities to the community of Waxhaw and surrounding areas in an inclusive and wholesome spirit. Beyond its mainstage season, the company runs a dedicated Murder Mystery Troupe offering interactive murder mystery performances. The 2026-2027 season features works by playwright Neil Simon alongside an original piece by a local artist.

name: Sampson Community Theatre
bio: Sampson Community Theatre is a non-profit organization run by a volunteer board, with a mission to provide arts and quality programs to the communities in and around Sampson County, NC. The theatre encourages participation and support from residents in theatre arts through productions and educational programs throughout its season at a great value, with all tickets priced at $15. SCT stages a full season of musicals, plays, and family productions at its home theatre in downtown Clinton, and gives weekly updates in two local newspapers, The Sampson Independent and The Sampson Weekly.

name: Theatre Guild of Rockingham County (TGRC)
bio: The Theatre Guild of Rockingham County, known as TGRC, began in 1989 as an extension of the Rockingham County High School drama program through the vision of founder Gene Saunders, opening with Bye Bye Birdie. The Guild grew from one show a year to a traditional four-show season, added a Children's Theatre for ages 8-14 in the 2000-2001 season, followed by Storybook Theater short plays for young children and a youth theatre program for ages 13-18. A summer theatre camp program was added in recent years, along with a mission to create, cultivate, and collaborate. In 2023 TGRC produced its first Black Theatre show, A Raisin in the Sun, and now includes at least one diversity show each season to serve all of Rockingham County. The company is currently in its 38th season, themed 'Come Alive.'

name: Myrtle Beach Area Children's Theater (MBACT)
bio: Myrtle Beach Area Children's Theater, known as Myrtle Beach ACT, offers performing arts education and student productions for the Grand Strand under the motto "Quality Instruction in an Encouraging Environment." Founded by Artistic Director Haley Morgan, a Myrtle Beach native, NYU Tisch School of the Arts graduate, and former Radio City Rockette, the company has been staging student productions since 2017. Its leveled performance classes run from the Shining Stars class for grades K-2 through the audition-based Step Up program for ages 14-19, and each session ends in a full production. MBACT also runs a pre-professional Company Theater program, a dance program for ages 5-19 with a competition team, a vocal studio, private lessons, and school-day performances, and it has just launched its first technical theater class.

name: RhinoLeap Productions
bio: RhinoLeap Productions is a professional theater company based in Asheboro, founded in 2015 by Tom and Patrick Osteen. The name reflects the founders' idea of something ancient doing something unexpected, and the company promises productions that are entertaining, thoughtful, and made with care. Led by Artistic Director Patrick Osteen, Executive Director Jeremy Skidmore, and Associate Artistic Director Kira Geiger, RhinoLeap stages immersive and intimate live productions in Asheboro, such as an actor-driven Little Women in a renovated barn, and takes shows on the road across the Triad, including an annual holiday radio play co-produced with 88.5 WFDD. The company also offers digital programming, the RhinoLeap Academy for education, and a membership program, and it is supported in part by the North Carolina Arts Council.

name: Mauldin Theatre Company
bio: Mauldin Theatre Company is the theatre program of the City of Mauldin's Mauldin Cultural Center, which has long served as a home for the performing arts. In 2017 the center became the base of the newly formed Mauldin Youth Theatre, which opened with Disney's The Lion King JR., and its performing arts offerings have since grown to include more youth theatre, musical revues and a community theatre that casts both adult and youth actors. The company produces a full season at the Cultural Center, adds free Spotlight Series productions at the city's outdoor amphitheater, offers arts education classes, and invites the community to join its production teams and volunteer crews.
